solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Small pot

definitions.meaning: first meaning: ...-sized, as in a ... edition or ... calculator
second meaning: in snooker or billiards, to send a ball into a hole at the table's edge

explanation.walkthrough: The two words read as a little cooking pot, but they are separate meanings: an attributive adjective and a snooker verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Pocket as a modifier means miniature, and to pocket a ball is to pot it in snooker.

clue.text: Girl with Bird is a typical example

parts.note: Pat is a girl's name
a tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: A girl and her bird are held up as a model case.
explanation.definitionFit: A pattern is a model or exemplar, something that serves as a typical specimen to copy.

clue.text: Curry favour with eccentric queen perhaps

parts.note: to court someone is to seek their favour
a card is an amusing, eccentric person

explanation.surface: Someone sucking up to an oddball monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Queen perhaps' looks like a monarch, but the perhaps marks it as one example of a playing card.
explanation.definitionFit: Court cards are the king, queen and jack in a pack of playing cards, so a queen is one.

clue.text: Surviving without Brown to face Tory leader

parts.note: ex means without, as in ex dividend
tan is a light brown colour

indicators.note: the leader is whoever comes first, so only the opening letter is kept

parts.note: the first letter of Tory

explanation.surface: Political survival without Gordon Brown, now confronting the Conservative leader.
explanation.walkthrough: Brown suggests the former Labour prime minister Gordon Brown; Tory is the everyday name for a British Conservative.
explanation.definitionFit: Extant means still existing, not lost or destroyed, so it is a synonym of surviving.

clue.text: The sort of worker who barely makes a living

definitions.text: The sort of worker who barely makes a living

parts.note: surface reading: a poorly paid worker who scrapes by on low wages
setter's reading: a performer who earns money by ending up bare, undressing on stage

explanation.walkthrough: 'Barely' suggests hardship and low pay; read literally it means while unclothed, which points to an undressing entertainer.
explanation.definitionFit: A striptease artiste is a worker whose income comes from removing clothes, so she literally earns while bare.

clue.text: Band's pointless journey

indicators.note: pointless means lacking a compass point, so one such letter is taken away

parts.note: a band is a strip of material

explanation.surface: A musical group's tour that achieved nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: S, for south, is the compass point dropped from the front of STRIP.
explanation.definitionFit: A trip is a short journey or outing from one place to another.

clue.text: It's natural at this time to support trendy conservationists

indicators.note: in a down answer, a support sits below, so the earlier part comes after what it holds up

parts.note: in means fashionable
here can mean at this point or moment
the National Trust, a British charity that conserves historic houses and countryside

explanation.surface: Backing fashionable green campaigners now comes naturally.
explanation.definitionFit: Inherent means existing as a natural, built-in part of something, so innately natural.

clue.text: Identify soft fabric

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical direction for soft
lace is a delicate openwork fabric

explanation.surface: An instruction to name a gentle textile.
explanation.definitionFit: To place someone is to recognise them and recall where you know them from.

clue.text: Ever so large rum bottle

indicators.note: rum as an adjective means odd or peculiar, so the letters come out strange

parts.note: taken as written, for rearranging
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A very big bottle of rum.
explanation.walkthrough: Rum and bottle both suggest drink; rum is the anagram signal and bottle is British slang for courage.
explanation.definitionFit: Bottle in British slang means nerve or courage, and resolve is firm determination.

clue.text: Hear about American president finally being faithful

indicators.note: about means going around, so one word wraps the others

parts.note: to hear a case in court is to try it
standard abbreviation for American

indicators.note: finally keeps only the closing letter of the word it follows

parts.note: the last letter of president

explanation.surface: An instruction to listen to stories of a US president who stayed loyal to the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hear' suggests listening, but here it is the legal sense: a judge hears a case.
explanation.definitionFit: A trusty friend is reliable and loyal, a close synonym of faithful.

clue.text: Service area in Mississippi sheltered by lofty trees at the rear

indicators.note: in places one item inside the state abbreviation that follows it
sheltered by puts the pair between the words on either side of it, one before and one after

parts.note: lofty means tall or high
the postal abbreviation for the state of Mississippi
standard abbreviation for area

indicators.note: at the rear keeps only the back letter of the word it follows

parts.note: the last letter of trees

explanation.surface: A rest area in Mississippi shaded by tall trees behind it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Service area' looks like a motorway stop, but the definition is 'Service' alone, a church service.
explanation.definitionFit: A High Mass is a full sung Eucharist, a church service with music and incense.

clue.text: Graceful animal deprived of watering hole for good

indicators.note: deprived of means having something taken away
for means in exchange for, so one item replaces the other

parts.note: a large animal
PH is the abbreviation for public house, a pub
standard abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: A graceful creature permanently barred from its drinking pool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Watering hole' suits an animal at a pool, but here it is the British slang for a pub, and 'for good' means swapping in G rather than forever.
explanation.definitionFit: Elegant means stylish and graceful in appearance or movement.

clue.text: Catch fish with cast net

indicators.note: cast suggests throwing something out so that it lands in a new arrangement

parts.note: the three letters rearranged
to fish with a rod and line is to angle

explanation.surface: Advice on catching fish by throwing out a net.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged letters of net come first, followed by the fishing verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To entangle is to trap or snare something so it cannot get free, as a net catches a fish.

clue.text: Desai ignoring the odds during amazing Lord's test

indicators.note: during means within the span of, so one piece sits inside the other
something amazing has been thrown into confusion, so its letters are jumbled
ignoring the odd-numbered letters keeps only the second, fourth and so on

parts.note: the even-positioned letters of Desai
the four letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Cricket talk: an Indian batsman named Desai struggling through a Test match at Lord's.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord's is the London cricket ground, and a Test is an international match, which makes 'test' look like part of the cricket scene.
explanation.definitionFit: An ordeal is a severe trial or painful experience, so it is a test of endurance.

clue.text: Extremely popular energy minister to make a false claim

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremes, the outermost letters of the word

parts.note: the first and last letters of popular
E is the physics symbol for energy
to minister to someone is to tend them

explanation.surface: A very well-liked energy minister fibbing about something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minister' looks like a political noun alongside 'energy'; it is the verb for caring.
explanation.definitionFit: To pretend is to claim falsely or put on a show of something untrue.

clue.text: Almost new organ

parts.note: standard abbreviation for new
the ear is an organ of hearing

explanation.surface: A church organ that is nearly brand new.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Organ' suggests the musical instrument; here it is a body part.
explanation.definitionFit: Near can be an adverb meaning nearly, as in a near perfect score.

clue.text: Advance of one thousand pounds is received in time

indicators.note: something received is taken in, so these letters go inside the word that follows

parts.note: an age is a period of time
a grand is slang for a thousand pounds or dollars
taken as written

explanation.surface: A loan of a thousand pounds arriving in good time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Advance' looks like a noun for a loan of money; the definition is the verb meaning promote.
explanation.definitionFit: To aggrandise someone is to promote or raise them in power and rank, to advance them.

clue.text: Involve one with power to stop climate change

indicators.note: change tells you to alter the letters into a new order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: to stop is to plug a gap, sitting inside it

parts.note: the seven letters rearranged
P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: A call for one powerful person to halt global warming.
explanation.walkthrough: I followed by M(P)LICATE: the power symbol stops a gap in the rearranged climate.
explanation.definitionFit: To implicate someone is to show they are involved in something, usually a crime.

clue.text: In spite of expectations of support Rex is abandoned completely

indicators.note: something abandoned is left behind, so a letter is dropped

parts.note: a rafter is a beam supporting a roof
R is the abbreviation for Rex, king
all means completely, as in all alone

explanation.surface: Despite hopes of backing, a king called Rex is wholly deserted.
explanation.walkthrough: Rex is Latin for king, abbreviated R as on coins and in legal cases.
explanation.definitionFit: After all is an idiom meaning despite what was expected, as in he came after all.

clue.text: Not certain to get home on it after steering device gets stuck in river

indicators.note: getting stuck in something means ending up lodged inside it
after means following, so the word before it is placed second, behind the device

parts.note: to be in is to be at home
the Dee is a river in Scotland and in Wales
a fin keeps a fish, rocket or surfboard on course
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone unsure whether they'll make it home after a boat's rudder jams in a river.
explanation.walkthrough: A fin is not literally a rudder, but it keeps fish, rockets and surfboards on course, so steering device is fair.
explanation.definitionFit: Indefinite means vague or not settled, so it is a fair synonym for not certain.

clue.text: Vet discovering ill-treated pets in Cuba

indicators.note: something ill-treated is knocked about, so its letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written, for rearranging
taken as written, for rearranging
C is the international vehicle registration code for Cuba

explanation.surface: An animal doctor finding mistreated pets on a visit to Cuba.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vet' reads as the animal doctor, fitting pets; it is the verb for checking.
explanation.definitionFit: To vet something is to examine it carefully, which is exactly what inspect means.

clue.text: Concealed in this particular box

indicators.note: concealed in says the letters lie tucked away inside the words that follow

parts.note: runs across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: Something hidden in a specific box.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Box' reads as a container noun, which suits 'concealed'; it is the verb for boxing.
explanation.definitionFit: To spar is to box, especially in practice bouts with a training partner.

clue.text: A politician appears in Vogue causing storm

indicators.note: appearing in something means showing up within it

parts.note: a rage is a craze or fashion, the vogue
taken as written
Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A politician features in the fashion magazine and stirs up a scandal.
explanation.walkthrough: Vogue looks like the magazine; lower-cased it means a craze.
explanation.definitionFit: To rampage is to rush about violently, which is to storm around.

clue.text: Force Frenchmen out of business

indicators.note: out of means removed from, so letters leave the word that follows

parts.note: commerce is business or trade
MM is the abbreviation for Messieurs, the French for gentlemen

explanation.surface: Forcing French workers out of their companies.
explanation.walkthrough: MM is removed from the middle of COMMERCE.
explanation.definitionFit: To coerce is to compel someone by force or threats.

clue.text: Holy city located in Swaziland

indicators.note: located in places one thing inside the boundaries of another

parts.note: SD was Swaziland's international vehicle registration code
Acre is a port city in northern Israel

explanation.surface: A sacred city found in the southern African kingdom of Swaziland.
explanation.walkthrough: S(ACRE)D: the city sits inside the country's code.
explanation.definitionFit: Sacred and holy both describe something consecrated or set apart for God.

clue.text: Colombia's incorporating socialist beliefs

definitions.note: plural definition for a singular noun; a credo is a set of beliefs

indicators.note: incorporating means taking into its body, so it holds the next item inside

parts.note: CO is the international code for Colombia
a red is a socialist or communist

explanation.surface: A Colombian political creed that takes in left-wing views.
explanation.walkthrough: C(RED)O.
explanation.definitionFit: A credo is a statement of the beliefs or principles that guide someone.

clue.text: Praise for ideas originally introduced to troubled commune

indicators.note: troubled means disturbed and stirred up, so the letters are scrambled
originally points to the starting letter of the word before it

parts.note: the first letter of ideas
taken as written, for rearranging

explanation.surface: Fresh ideas being brought to a commune in difficulty earn applause.
explanation.walkthrough: The single letter is added to commune and the whole lot is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: An encomium is a formal speech or piece of writing that lavishly praises someone.

clue.text: Failing to complete crazy flying stunt

indicators.note: failing to complete means stopping short, so the final letter is lost

parts.note: loopy is slang for crazy

explanation.surface: A mad aerobatic manoeuvre that a pilot doesn't manage to finish.
explanation.walkthrough: The Y at the end of LOOPY is dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: A loop the loop is an aerobatic manoeuvre in which a plane flies a vertical circle.

clue.text: It's essential to compel Eva to refuse a lift

indicators.note: essential to means forming the core of, so the letters sit inside the words that follow

parts.note: runs from the end of compel through Eva and to into the start of refuse

explanation.surface: A man who must make Eva turn down an offer of a ride home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lift' reads as a ride in a car; it is the British word for the machine Americans call by this name.
explanation.definitionFit: An elevator is the American name for a lift, a cage that carries people between floors.

clue.text: American soldiers withholding container's secrets

parts.note: standard abbreviation for American

indicators.note: withholding means keeping something back, held inside

parts.note: the Royal Artillery, a British army regiment
a can is a tin container

explanation.surface: US troops keeping back the secrets inside a shipping container.
explanation.walkthrough: A followed by R(CAN)A.
explanation.definitionFit: Arcana are mysteries or deep secrets known only to the initiated.

clue.text: Writer's old lines filled with irony — maybe just the opposite

indicators.note: something filled with stuff holds it inside
just the opposite swaps which piece is the filling and which the shell

parts.note: irony is an example of a figure of speech, signalled by maybe
standard abbreviation for old
L is the abbreviation for line, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: A writer's old lines seem laced with irony, or perhaps the reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface says the lines hold the irony; 'just the opposite' turns it round so the irony holds the lines. Anthony Trollope was a Victorian novelist.
explanation.definitionFit: Anthony Trollope, author of the Barsetshire novels, is a famous English novelist, so a writer.

clue.text: Always cutting about this American patriot

indicators.note: cutting into something means going inside it

parts.note: re means about or concerning
ever means always

explanation.surface: A patriotic American who is forever cutting a dash.
explanation.walkthrough: R(EVER)E.
explanation.definitionFit: Paul Revere was the silversmith patriot famous for his midnight ride warning of British troops.
